summary:
### TL;DR
- **GitHub-hosted runner IP ranges are not dedicated to Actions.** The docs now say the `actions` ranges from `GET /meta` cover the broader address space of the cloud provider regions the runners use. Allowlisting these ranges trusts more than your runners. ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners))
- **AI Scan for repositories can now be started in bulk** for up to 20 repositories at once. It is in public preview and does not require a Copilot license. ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-16-bulk-start-ai-scan-for-repositories))
- **Actions workflow execution protection docs no longer list plan restrictions.** The "Evaluate" enforcement mode is no longer marked as GitHub Enterprise Cloud only. ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/administer/control-workflow-execution))
- **The VS Code Local harness for Copilot agent sessions will be removed in February 2027.** Admins should move to the Copilot harness, which supports managed runtime permissions and sandbox restrictions. ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-16-vs-code-retires-the-local-harness-in-february-2027))

### Action required
- **VS Code Local harness removal (February 2027):**
  - VS Code 1.146 deprecates the Local harness. Users should select **Copilot** under Session Target and check their customizations for compatibility.
  - Admins should review any `vscode.temporaryDefaultToLocalHarness` exception. That setting will be removed along with the Local harness, so keeping it won't preserve the Local harness.
  - Admins should also verify workflows, permission controls and sandbox configuration with the Copilot harness. Selecting the Copilot harness does not enable sandboxing by itself.
  - [Source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-16-vs-code-retires-the-local-harness-in-february-2027)
- **Copilot models deprecated as of 2026-11-16:**
  - Claude Opus 4.8 and Claude Opus 5 → use Claude Opus 5.5.
  - GPT-5.6 Terra → use GPT-6.1 Sol or GPT-6 Luna.
  - Update any workflows or integrations that pin these models.
  - If you turned off the global default model enablement, you must enable the alternatives manually.
  - [Source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-16-github-copilot-models-deprecated-on-november-16-2026)
- **Review runner IP allowlists.** Keep allowlists in sync with all ranges in the `actions` array. Allowlists limited to Azure or Microsoft ranges, including Entra Conditional Access policies, can block runners from the multi-cloud Linux pool. [Source](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners)

### Security improvements
- **Bulk start for AI Scan for repositories (public preview).**
  - Scans the default branch, covering languages CodeQL doesn't support and finding extra issues in languages it does.
  - Findings appear alongside CodeQL alerts.
  - You can start scans when you enable the org setting or from the org-level code scanning alerts page.
  - Available on github.com and GHE Cloud with data residency.
  - [Changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-16-bulk-start-ai-scan-for-repositories), [docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/secure-at-scale/configure-organization-security/establish-complete-coverage/configure-global-settings)
- **Dependabot delegated alert dismissal requests now stay open for one year instead of one week.** This is live on github.com and will ship in GHES 3.24. [Source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-16-dependabot-alert-dismissal-requests-now-last-one-year)

### Docs changes worth reading
- **Workflow execution protections:**
  - The page no longer restricts the feature to public repos and Team/Enterprise private repos.
  - "Evaluate" mode, which lets you monitor would-be violations in policy insights, is no longer labeled GHEC-only.
  - [Docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/administer/control-workflow-execution)
- **`ACTIONS_CACHE_MODE` scope:**
  - The variable is set only for JavaScript and Docker container actions.
  - It is not available to `run` steps, including `run` steps inside composite actions.
  - Custom cache logic in shell steps therefore can't read the effective cache mode from it.
  - [Docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching)
- **Reusable workflow contexts corrected:**
  - `jobs.<job_id>.with.*` now allows `github`, `needs`, `strategy`, `matrix`, `inputs` and `vars`. Previously the docs listed only `github` and `needs`.
  - `jobs.<job_id>.secrets.*` now also allows `strategy`, `matrix`, `inputs` and `vars`.
  - [Workflow syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax), [contexts](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts)
- **`workflow_dispatch` inputs:** `description`, `default` and `options` are now documented.
  - A `choice` input's default must be one of its `options`.
  - Defining `options` on any non-`choice` input makes the workflow invalid, and it fails to run.
  - [Docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax)
- **New `issues` activity type:** `status_changed` is now listed as a trigger, on versions that support issue status webhooks. [Docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows)
- **Dependabot and private Swift dependencies:** the org-level "Grant Dependabot access to private repositories" setting does not cover Swift. Configure a `git` registry with credentials in `dependabot.yml` instead. [Docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/secure-at-scale/configure-organization-security/establish-complete-coverage/configure-global-settings)
- **Secret scanning historical scan notifications:** owners and security managers are now emailed only when a historical scan generated alerts, not on every completed scan. Don't treat the absence of an email as proof a scan ran. [Docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/manage-security-alerts/manage-secret-scanning-alerts/monitoring-alerts)

changelog.title: Dependabot alert dismissal requests now last one year
changelog.text: If you use delegated alert dismissal for Dependabot , dismissal requests now stay open for one year instead of one week. Reviewers have more time to respond before a request expires and has to be resubmitted. This change is available on github.com and will ship in GitHub Enterprise Server 3.24. The post Dependabot alert dismissal requests now last one year appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

changelog.title: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — November 9
changelog.text: This week, bring GitHub Enterprise Server repositories into the Copilot app and see which agent sessions need you first in VS Code. You can also try two new models, Claude Fable 5.2 and Gemini 4 Carbon. GitHub Copilot Claude Fable 5.2 is available to Copilot Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise users. It requires data retention by default, and Copilot Business and Enterprise administrators must turn on its policy, which is off by default. Learn more about Claude Fable 5.2 . Gemini 4 Carbon is available to Copilot Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise users. GitHub Copilot app Continue cloud and Codespace sessions on your phone. A new Open in menu includes a GitHub Mobile option that shows a QR code. Sign back in to MCP servers such as Slack without leaving the conversation. When a server needs you to sign in again, the conversation offers the matching connector, connects it in place, and resumes your task. Work with repositories, issues, and pull requests from GitHub Enterprise Server in the Copilot app, now generally available. You’ll still need a GitHub.com or GHE.com account, and cloud sessions aren’t available for GHES. Learn more about signing in with GHES . Schedule Project automations down to the minute, or use a custom cron schedule such as weekdays at 9:30. Dictate in French, Spanish, and other languages. Download the multilingual voice model in settings, then choose Auto or a specific language. Filter issues and pull requests by custom fields, such as a GitHub Project’s Size, from the Add filter menu. Combine high contrast with red, green, or blue-yellow color filters in Settings > Accessibility , and preview combinations before you apply them. High contrast replaces the separate “Increase contrast” setting. You can also choose GitHub Dimmed as a dark-only palette in Settings > Themes . Install the GitHub Copilot app . GitHub Copilot in VS Code (1.146 release) Let an agent run model comparisons for you. With Compare Models enabled, turn on the agent tools in settings, and agents can find available models, launch comparisons, and read the results to summarize findings. This is experimental. Track agent sessions across all your workspaces from one view with Inbox mode in the Agents window’s sessions list. Sessions that need your attention appear first, and you can dismiss, hold, or snooze the rest. This is experimental. Move a chat out of the Agents window into its own window, then arrange the chat, its editors, and its terminals to fit the task. Chat windows are in preview. Find, install, and uninstall extensions without leaving the Agents window. Extensions with unsupported features show a warning before you install them. This is experimental. Move to the Copilot harness before the Local harness is removed in February 2027. The Copilot harness is already the default for new sessions, and the transition guide covers moving any remaining workflows. Explore everything that’s new in the full release notes . The post GitHub Copilot weekly releases — November 9 appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

changelog.title: GitHub Copilot models deprecated on November 16, 2026
changelog.text: As of today, November 16, 2026, we have deprecated the following models across most GitHub Copilot experiences (including Copilot Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions). Note that Claude Opus 4.8 is still available to individual GitHub Copilot subscribers on annual plans. These deprecations were announced on October 15, 2026 . Model Deprecation date Suggested alternative Claude Opus 4.8 2026-11-16 Claude Opus 5.5 Claude Opus 5 2026-11-16 Claude Opus 5.5 GPT-5.6 Terra 2026-11-16 GPT-6.1 Sol or GPT-6 Luna Claude Opus 5 has been removed from the model picker but remains available for runtime refusal fallback through existing authorized access. Existing enterprise model policies continue to apply. Please update your workflows and integrations to use supported models. Under default model enablement, the suggested alternatives are automatically enabled for Copilot Enterprise and Copilot Business customers unless an administrator has turned off the global default or explicitly disabled the model. If you’ve turned off the global default, you can enable access to the alternative models through their model policies in Copilot settings. Once enabled, users will see the model in the Copilot Chat model selector in supported GitHub Copilot experiences. No action is required to remove the deprecated models. GitHub Enterprise customers with questions or concerns are encouraged to reach out to their account manager for further assistance. Share your feedback To learn more about the models available in Copilot, see our documentation on models and get started with Copilot today. Join the GitHub Community to share your feedback. The post GitHub Copilot models deprecated on November 16, 2026 appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

changelog.title: VS Code retires the Local harness in February 2027
changelog.text: Visual Studio Code 1.146 deprecates the Local harness, the older software that coordinates the model, context, and tools for GitHub Copilot agent sessions in the editor. The Local harness will be removed in February 2027. Its replacement, the Microsoft Copilot harness , is built into VS Code and has been the default for new sessions since VS Code 1.143. You can keep working in VS Code and running agent commands on your machine. Choosing the Copilot harness doesn’t move your files to the cloud. During the three-month transition, the Local harness remains available where your organization’s policy permits. However, new features and improvements will focus on the Copilot harness. Why use the Copilot harness Built on the Copilot SDK , the Copilot harness shares its coding-agent runtime with Copilot CLI and the GitHub Copilot app. You can continue the same session between the editor and the Agents window in VS Code while the session’s Agent Host process stays running. Editor-provided tools still require a connected editor. With the Copilot harness, you can: Let Copilot Fusion choose models and, on supported tiers, coordinate drafting and review for your task. Reduce approval interruptions with assisted permissions . Calls that are not approved by the risk assessment will still come to you for confirmation. Bring context from your team’s services using Copilot connectors , without configuring MCP servers yourself. Connectors are in preview. Plan work on task boards and explore interactive diagrams with canvases , which are in preview. If you access models through GitHub Copilot, you can continue to use your existing plan, including Copilot Free. Individual features and Fusion tiers depend on your plan, settings, and organization policy. With the Copilot harness, administrators can enforce managed runtime permissions and sandbox restrictions that the Local harness cannot enforce. Configure these controls separately; selecting the Copilot harness doesn’t enable sandboxing. What you need to do If you still use the Local harness, start a new session in VS Code and select Copilot under Session Target . Review your customizations for compatibility before February 2027. Switching harnesses doesn’t automatically convert every customization. If you administer VS Code, review any vscode.temporaryDefaultToLocalHarness exception and verify your required workflows, permission controls, and sandbox configuration with the Copilot harness before February 2027. The temporary enterprise-managed setting will be removed along with the Local harness, so keeping the exception configured won’t keep the Local harness available. Follow the Local harness transition guide . If a workflow blocks your move, report a VS Code issue . The post VS Code retires the Local harness in February 2027 appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

changelog.title: Bulk start AI Scan for repositories
changelog.text: AI Scan for repositories finds security vulnerabilities on your repository’s default branch. It covers languages CodeQL doesn’t support and finds additional issues in languages CodeQL already analyzes. Findings appear in your code scanning backlog alongside CodeQL alerts. You can now start AI Scans for up to 20 repositories at once. Start scans for selected repositories when you enable the organization-level setting, or from the code scanning organization alerts page. You can also start a scan for an individual repository from its alerts page. Bulk start for AI Scan for repositories is in public preview. AI Scan for repositories is available on github.com and GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency. A GitHub Copilot license isn’t required. Learn more about AI Scan and join the discussion in GitHub Community . The post Bulk start AI Scan for repositories appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

 The runner exposes the effective mode in the `ACTIONS_CACHE_MODE` environment variable, and the `actions/cache` action and the `@actions/cache` toolkit honor it. Restore is skipped when the mode does not allow reads (`none` or `write-only`), and save is skipped when the mode does not allow writes (`none` or `read`). docs.title: Clarify that ACTIONS_CACHE_MODE is not set for run steps (#46906)

files.patch:
@@ -314,6 +314,9 @@ For the trusted-versus-low-trust trigger breakdown, see [Cache access for low-tr
 
 The runner exposes the effective mode in the `ACTIONS_CACHE_MODE` environment variable, and the `actions/cache` action and the `@actions/cache` toolkit honor it. Restore is skipped when the mode does not allow reads (`none` or `write-only`), and save is skipped when the mode does not allow writes (`none` or `read`). When a cache operation is skipped because of the mode, the action logs an informational message and the step and run continue without failing. A skipped restore is treated as a cache miss; a skipped save is simply not performed.
 
+> [!NOTE]
+> `ACTIONS_CACHE_MODE` is only set in the environment of JavaScript and Docker container actions. It is not available to `run` steps, including `run` steps in composite actions.
+
 ### Cache access in reusable workflows
 
 `cache-mode` propagates from a caller workflow to the reusable workflows it calls. An explicit `cache-mode` on the calling job, or inherited from the caller workflow, limits the cache access the called workflow can request.
